Belgium

27 ads · €4978 spend · 193 purchases
✅ What's Working
• The lone Carousel (Carousel_120237873305580396 - Copy) is the undisputed volume winner: 66 purchases, 8.95x ROAS, €18 CPP at highest spend — proof this format scales hard in BE.
• Product-specific statics deliver outsized ROAS on modest spend: Diamond Earstud #4 (18.31x, €7.95 CPP), Edge #1 (10.68x), WCDxBA #5 (10.42x). Clear, hero-product-focused creative wins every time.
• The WCDxBA collab concept is the most consistently profitable idea in the account — all three variants are profitable (#5 at 10.42x, #1 at 5.20x, #2 at 3.40x). Rare consistency.
❌ What's Not Working
• Partner creatives are a money pit: Partner #4 lost money at 0.64x ROAS (€116 for 1 purchase), Partner #3 barely converts at 1.25x despite a 412% CTR. High clicks, no buyers — the landing experience or offer isn't matching the creative promise.
• Generic video and UGC concepts underperform badly: Video _ Creative #3 burned €197 at 1.22x, and Static _ UGC #2 spent €201 at 1.73x with a €67 CPP. These lack the product specificity that drives conversion in this market.
⬆ Double Down On
• Build more carousels immediately. You have ONE carousel and it's your #1 ad by every metric. Create carousel variants around Diamond Earstud, Heart Tag, Edge, and WCDxBA — you're leaving money on the table.
• Scale the product-hero static formula. Diamond Earstud #4 and Edge #1 prove that single-product, benefit-clear statics convert at 10-18x ROAS. Produce 3-4 variants per top SKU with angle variations (price anchor, social proof, close-up detail).
• Expand the WCDxBA concept into new formats: video walkthroughs, carousels, UGC-style reviews. Three statics all profitable is a signal to go all-in on this collab.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Pause Static _ Partner #4 today — 0.64x ROAS means you're paying Meta to lose money. No redemption path.
• Kill Video _ Creative #3 — €197 at 1.22x with only 4 purchases. The creative concept is dead, stop feeding it budget.
• Shut down Static _ UGC #2 — €67 CPP is 8.4x worse than Diamond Earstud #4. Generic UGC without a product hero doesn't work in BE.

🇩🇪

Germany

3 ads · €1065 spend · 9 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Video format is the only format generating purchases in DE — both Video _ Stack #1 (6 purch.) and Video _ Kay #1 (3 purch.) converted, while static did not.
• Video _ Kay #1 is the most capital-efficient ad at €82.44 CPP and 1.59x ROAS on only €247 spend — strongest signal in the account.
• CTRs are healthy across all three ads (1.66–1.99%), meaning the creative hooks are engaging; the bottleneck is post-click conversion, not attention.
❌ What's Not Working
• Static _ Earstud New #1 spent €131 with zero purchases — high CTR but no conversions means interest without intent; the creative likely lacks a clear value prop or purchase driver.
• Video _ Stack #1 consumed the most budget (€687) yet returned only 1.26x ROAS with a bloated €114.42 CPP — it is the biggest cash drain in Germany.
• No ad in the entire DE market clears even 2x ROAS; the market has no proven winner to scale, only weak signals to iterate on.
⬆ Double Down On
• Iterate on the Kay concept: it has the best efficiency ratio in DE. Produce 3-4 new variants (different hooks, lengths, CTAs) to find a scalable winner.
• Introduce UGC for the German market — zero UGC exists in the current mix, and peer-driven content typically lowers CPP for affordable-luxury jewelry among 18-35 women.
• Test German-language ad copy and on-screen text; all current creative appears untailored — localized messaging could close the post-click conversion gap.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill Static _ Earstud New #1 immediately — €131 gone, zero signal, no reason to let it eat another euro.
• Stop feeding Video _ Stack #1 at its current form — €687 for 1.26x ROAS is a slow bleed. Pause and rework the concept before reintroducing.

AI

Creative Analysis

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €3073 spend · 361 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Static ads utterly dominate: 'Berekening #2' delivers 45.27x ROAS at €3.12 CPP, 'Code #1' hits 32.85x ROAS — every top performer is a static image, not video.
• Value-framing and promo code concepts convert hardest. 'Berekening' (cost calculation), 'Code' (discount code), and 'Weather #2' (€4.26 CPP) prove rational buying triggers crush emotional brand content.
• Artist-specific statics convert: 'RUBEN' at 20.29x ROAS and €6.70 CPP outperforms generic event creatives by 3-6x on efficiency.
❌ What's Not Working
• Video is a budget drain. 'Aftermovie #1' converts at €24.56 CPP (3x the static average). Both McDrummer videos spent €50 combined with zero purchases despite 900-1150% CTRs — entertainment that sells nothing.
• 'Organic #1' is a vanity trap: 1287% CTR, €50 spent, zero conversions. Maximum clicks, zero purchase intent.
• 'Waar vo #1' (original) has a catastrophic €34.61 CPP and 3.53x ROAS while its copy variant performs 3x better — should have been killed weeks ago.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more 'Berekening'-style value breakdowns — the single best concept in the account (45.27x ROAS). Test cost-per-hour, cost-vs-a-night-out, cost-vs-other-festivals angles.
• Scale promo code statics aggressively — both 'Code #1' variants run 15-33x ROAS. Create fresh code creatives with urgency countdown layers.
• Build an artist spotlight series replicating the 'RUBEN' format for every headliner. Individual artist call-outs clearly outperform generic lineup or brand creative.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all video ads immediately. Aftermovie and McDrummer concepts collectively spent €197 for 6 total purchases at €32.83 CPP. The 'video-first' strategy is objectively wrong — statics outsell video 10:1 on efficiency.
• Pause 'Organic #1' — zero commercial value despite massive engagement. Misleading creative or wrong audience.
• Sunset 'Waar vo #1' (original) — a better-performing copy variant already exists. No reason to keep the inferior version burning budget at €34.61 CPP.

Creative Analysis

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no results

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €13046 spend · 298 results
✅ What's Working
• Vergelijking (comparison) format is the undeniable engine — 'Static _ Vergelijking #2 - Copy' alone drove 91 leads at €39.91 CPR, and 'Static _ Vergelijking #1 - Copy' variants hit €26-32 CPR with strong volume. Broker-vs-kleyo fee framing converts.
• Press credibility punches above its weight — 'Static _ De Tijd 2 - Copy' delivered €14.40 CPR on limited spend, the best cost/result in the account by 2x.
• 'General Video #1' proves video works at scale (€37.43 CPR, 20 results) — motion adds legitimacy to the cost-savings narrative.
❌ What's Not Working
• Poll creatives are dead weight — 'Static _ Poll #2 - Copy 2' at €73.36 CPR and 'Static _ Poll #2 - Copy' at €50.72 CPR with only 6 combined leads. Engagement-bait format doesn't convert homeowners.
• 'Smart' and 'Zelf Verkopen' concepts flopped — €94-85 CPR with 1 result each. Messaging is too vague to drive action.
• Duplicate copies are cannibalizing — the bad variant of 'Static _ Vergelijking #2 - Copy 2' burned €742 for 5 leads (€148.45 CPR) while the good variant ran alongside it. Same story with the weak 'General Video #1 - Copy' at €152.71 CPR.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce 3-4 new comparison static variants — test different price anchors (€300K home = €9,000 broker vs €1,800 kleyo), different visual layouts, different copy hooks. This format has proven product-market fit.
• Scale the press/media proof angle hard — the De Tijd creative is the lowest CPR in the account. Create variants featuring other press mentions, trust badges, third-party validation.
• Invest in more video — 'General Video #1' is efficient and scalable. Produce UGC-style seller testimonials and short explainer videos showing the process.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill the Poll format entirely — it's an engagement trap that doesn't convert to leads. €418 spent, 6 leads, zero scaling potential.
• Kill the 'Smart' concept — vague naming, vague results. Two variants, €181 spent, 2 leads. The concept isn't resonating.
• Kill the underperforming duplicate copies immediately — the bad 'Vergelijking #2 - Copy 2' (€148 CPR) and bad 'General Video #1 - Copy' (€152 CPR) are burning budget that should go to their winning siblings.

Belgium

16 ads · €4356 spend · 76 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Offer statics dominate: 'Static _ Offer #1 - Copy' is a 9.51x ROAS monster at €46.70 CPP — best efficiency in the account by far. The original 'Static _ Offer #1' also carries volume (25 purchases) proving the offer-led static format converts.
• Renée ambassador videos punch above weight: 'Video _ Renée #1 - Copy' delivers 3.98x ROAS at scale (16 purchases), and 'Video _ Renée #2 - Copy' shows 3.68x ROAS with the lowest CPP in the account (€33.94) — authentic creator content clearly resonates.
• Product-focused statics quietly efficient: 'Static _ Product Ziris #2' delivers a solid €45.86 CPP on just €183 spend, proving that clean product creative can convert without heavy discounting.
❌ What's Not Working
• Offer fatigue is real: 'Static _ Offer #2' (1.76x), '#3' (1.07x), and '#4' (0x) progressively collapse — you cannot just clone the offer format with weaker hooks and expect results. CPP balloons from €46 to €109+.
• Split-format videos are a conversion graveyard: 'Video _ Ziris Split #1' burned €116 with zero purchases, 'Ziris Split #2' another €39 for nothing, and both Sieben Splits spent €27 combined with zero conversions. The format simply does not close.
• Sieben UGC underdelivers despite massive engagement: 'Video _ Sieben UGC #1' has a 129% CTR but only 1.65x ROAS — clicks without purchase intent signal the wrong audience or weak post-click experience.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more Renée-style ambassador/testimonial videos — both Renée ads are top-3 on ROAS. Film new variants with different hooks, products (Helbo, Selva), and seasonal angles. This format is your best efficiency play.
• Iterate on the winning 'Offer #1' static with fresh visual treatments and angles (e.g., prescription USP, photochromic demo, Belgian-made angle) — the format works, but you need new hooks to fight creative fatigue instead of cloning weaker offers.
• Create more product-hero statics like 'Product Ziris #2' for the full range (Helbo, Selva Snow, jerseys) — clean product creative at low CPP diversifies your conversion sources beyond offer-dependency.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all split-format videos immediately — 5 ads, €288 spent, 2 total purchases. The format is structurally broken for this audience.
• Kill 'Static _ Offer #3' and '#4' — combined €268 for 2 purchases at 1.07x and 0x ROAS. Stop feeding losing offer variants; the budget belongs in the winning #1 copy.
• Stop spreading offer budget across weak variants. Consolidate into proven winners.

9 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

9 ads · €2278 spend · 110 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Catalog Carousel - Espresso Coffee is the undisputed engine: 27.75x ROAS, €13.67 CPP, 72 purchases — dynamic product ads with category specificity crush everything else.
• Segmented retargeting statics (Hold #1, Hold #2, Repeat #1) deliver the lowest CPPs in the account (€7.78–€19.37) proving lifecycle-based creative works beautifully.
• Origin storytelling converts quietly — Static _ Origin #1 hits 12.15x ROAS at €17.93 CPP on just €72 spend; provenance sells to this audience.
❌ What's Not Working
• Video _ OR Coffee is the biggest waste: €634 spent, 4 purchases, €158 CPP. High CTR means people watch but don't buy — brand vibes without a product hook don't convert.
• Static_Barista_Courses - Copy is off-strategy: selling courses in an e-commerce campaign yields 1 purchase at €89 CPP. Wrong product, wrong funnel.
• Carousel__Filter - Copy limps at 3.97x ROAS while the catalog carousel format hits 27.75x — manual carousels can't compete with dynamic catalog for product discovery.
⬆ Double Down On
• Category-specific catalog carousels: replicate the Espresso Carousel for filter, single origin, and subscription bundles — the format is proven, expand the catalog.
• Lifecycle-segmented statics: produce more Hold/Repeat/Never variants with fresh angles (origin, subscription, seasonal) — these are cheap converters starved of budget.
• Origin-first storytelling: Static _ Origin #1 proves this audience pays for provenance — build a series around specific farms, processing methods, and harvest seasons.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill the current brand video format — €158 CPP for coffee beans is indefensible. If video stays, it needs a complete rebuild around product and conversion.
• Pull Static_Barista_Courses - Copy out of e-commerce campaigns immediately — courses belong in a separate awareness/lead-gen funnel, not competing for DPA budget.
• Stop spending on Carousel__Filter - Copy in its current form — the manual carousel format is objectively outclassed by catalog; rebuild as a dynamic catalog carousel instead.

🇧🇪

Belgium

4 ads · €751 spend · 48 results
✅ What's Working
• "Static _ Investeren _ 2" is a clear winner — 48 leads at €13.81 CPR on €663 spend with massive engagement (279.80% CTR). Investment angle resonates strongly with Belgian audience.
• Static format works for this audience — the top performer is a simple static creative, proving you don't need video to convert in Belgian real estate lead gen.
• The "Investeren" framing clearly hooks Belgian buyers — all four ads use this angle, and the one with enough spend and the right creative execution delivers results efficiently.
❌ What's Not Working
• "Static _ Investeren _ 3" burned €70 with zero results — high CTR (130.15%) but no conversions means the landing page or form doesn't match the creative promise.
• Creative diversity is nonexistent — four static investment ads is not a test strategy, it's one idea repeated. No lifestyle, no video, no second-home or kijkwoning angle tested.
• "Static _ Investeren _ 4" got almost no delivery (€3) — Meta's algorithm rejected it fast, likely due to weak creative signal or overlap with the winning variant.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more static investment creatives iterating on "Static _ Investeren _ 2" — test new headlines, imagery crops, and CTA variations to find the next winner before fatigue hits.
• Launch lifestyle and emotional waterfront creatives — the Westerschelde panoramic views and dijkdorp concept are untapped creative goldmines for Belgium's second-home seekers.
• Build a kijkwoning visit funnel with dedicated creatives — invite-style ads with property photography drive urgency and qualify high-intent leads at the top.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill "Static _ Investeren _ 3" immediately — €70 spent, zero results, classic click-trap with no conversion. The disconnect between click and lead means the creative overpromises or the LP underdelivers.
• Stop running four near-identical static investment ads simultaneously — you're cannibalizing your own auction and letting Meta split budget across losers.

Netherlands

6 ads · €1653 spend · 68 results
✅ What's Working
• Lifestyle-emotional creative crushes investment messaging — 'Static _ Water Wind _ Form' drives 52 leads at €21.84 CPR, proving the dreamy water/rust angle resonates with Dutch buyers.
• 'Video _ Lifestyle #1' is the hidden gem — lowest CPR (€16.70) and highest CTR (418.83%) on minimal spend. Video + lifestyle = your most efficient formula.
• Lead-gen forms paired with evocative visuals (water, wind, space) convert far better than rational investment pitches.
❌ What's Not Working
• The entire 'Investeren' static series is dragging — four variants averaging €35+ CPR when they convert at all. 'Static _ Investeren - Copy' and 'Static _ Investeren _ 4 - Copy' burned budget with zero results.
• Over-reliance on static format for the investment angle — rational messaging in static format lacks the emotional pull this audience needs.
• Too many near-identical 'Investeren' copy variants competing without meaningful creative differentiation. Four versions of the same weak angle is not a test, it's waste.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more video lifestyle content — drone shots, golden-hour Westerschelde footage, slow reveals of the dijkdorp. 'Video _ Lifestyle #1' proves this format converts at 30% lower CPR than your best static.
• Lean harder into the emotional territory of 'Water Wind' — the sensory, poetic angle (rust, ruimte, water) is your best-performing creative territory by far.
• Create kijkwoning-specific creative — the model home is your conversion event; build ads that sell the visit itself, not just the concept.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop producing more 'Investeren' static variants. Four copies of the same underperforming angle is creative debt, not testing.
• Kill the rational-first investment messaging as a primary hook — use it as a secondary frame within lifestyle-led creative instead.

11 ads · €3747 spend · 316 results
✅ What's Working
• Visit and water/wind lifestyle statics are lead machines — 'Static _ Visit #2 - Copy' (€7.85/lead, 96 results) and 'Static _ Water Wind _ Form' (€9.51/lead, 108 results) dominate volume and efficiency.
• Product-specific announcements crush it — 'Static _ Nieuw_App #1' delivers the cheapest leads at €6.83 across 22 results, proving new-inventory urgency works.
• Static formats with evocative nature/water imagery and direct form CTAs are the winning formula across the board.
❌ What's Not Working
• 'Static _ Review _ Form' is burning €1002 at a brutal €28.62/lead — 3x worse than top performers. Social proof angle is falling flat for this audience.
• Copy-variant strategy is inconsistent — 'Static _ Water Wind _ Form - Copy' costs €21.15/lead vs. the original's €9.51, and 'Static _ Nieuw_App #1 - Copy' at €15.65 is 2.3x worse than the original. Duplicating winners without iterating the creative kills efficiency.
• Video formats are essentially untested — 'Video _ Testimonial #1' and 'Video _ Lifestyle #1' got nearly zero spend, leaving a massive format gap unvalidated.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more water/nature landscape statics with form-fill CTAs — the Westerschelde panoramic view + emotional headline combo is proven gold.
• Lean into product-specific urgency formats (new phases, limited apartments, kijkwoning availability) — 'Nieuw_App' style announcements convert cheapest.
• Invest in video creative testing — drone flyovers, lifestyle walkthroughs, and resident testimonials are completely untapped and could unlock scale beyond statics.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill 'Static _ Review _ Form' immediately — €1002 spent at nearly 3x the avg CPL is unacceptable waste. Social proof isn't the conversion driver here.
• Kill 'Static _ Water Wind _ Form - Copy' and 'Static _ Visit #1' — both are inferior duplicates of better-performing originals eating budget.

Belgium

12 ads · €1703 spend · 329 results
✅ What's Working
• Bauhaus and Sommerfeld themes dominate: Bauhaus #5 (€4.83/result, 133 leads) and Sommerfeld #3 (€4.66/result, 86 leads) account for 68% of all results — Meta's algorithm is rightly funneling budget here.
• Sub-€5 cost per property lead is exceptional for luxury real estate; static imagery with clear modernist design references clearly resonates with the affluent Belgian coastal buyer.
• Several budget-starved ads show even stronger early signals — Bauhaus #1 (€3.15/result), Naoshima #3 (€1.65/result), Sommerfeld #2 (€4.22/result) — untapped potential the algorithm never had room to validate.
❌ What's Not Working
• Bauhaus #3 (€13.60/result) and Bauhaus #4 (€11.57/result) cost 2-3x the account average with a combined 3 leads — whatever angle these took within the Bauhaus theme is not landing.
• Naoshima #1 spent €6 with zero results — dead on arrival. The Naoshima theme overall runs 30-40% more expensive per lead than Bauhaus or Sommerfeld.
• Zero format diversity — 12 static ads, no video, no carousel. For modernist architecture on the Belgian coast, that's a massive missed opportunity.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more Bauhaus and Sommerfeld variants — these themes deliver 30-40% cheaper leads than Naoshima. Iterate on composition, crop, and copy around proven winners #5 and #3.
• Force budget into suppressed high-signal creatives (Bauhaus #1, Naoshima #3, Sommerfeld #2) — their early cost/result outperforms top spenders but they never got spend to validate.
• Introduce video and carousel formats: walkthrough tours, architectural detail sequences, coastal lifestyle reels. A product this visually rich should not be static-only.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Pause Bauhaus #3 and #4 immediately — €37 combined spend, 3 total leads at €12+ each. Five other Bauhaus variants beat them convincingly.
• Kill Naoshima #1 — zero results, zero signal, pulling impressions from winners.
• Stop running six Bauhaus variants simultaneously — consolidate budget behind the two proven ones and one test variant at most.

Other

10 ads · €51 spend · 1 purchases
✅ What's Working
• "Instagram post: New deliveries! Bekijk ons gamma..." is the only converter — 37.93x ROAS on just €22 spend. 'New arrivals' angle + product range CTA works.
• High CTR across most posts suggests strong visual engagement, meaning product imagery resonates even when copy is weak or missing.
• Dutch-language, Instagram-native formats feel organic and earn clicks — boosted post style outperforms blank or generic messages.
❌ What's Not Working
• Multiple ads running with literally no copy ("Bericht: ''") — zero strategy, zero conversions. Pure budget waste across at least 3 ads.
• "🦆 KLAAR VOOR DE OPENING OP 15..." spent €10 on an event announcement with no purchase path — awareness spend with no funnel.
• Scattershot approach: 10 ads, ~€50 total spend, no real testing structure. Budgets too thin to learn anything meaningful.
⬆ Double Down On
• 'New deliveries / new arrivals' angle with clear product showcase — the only proven converter. Build a repeatable template around this.
• Product-range browsing CTAs ('Bekijk ons gamma') that push to shop — replicate the winning ad's structure with fresh product drops.
• Instagram-native lifestyle imagery paired with urgency copy — lean into the organic engagement this audience already delivers.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• All blank-copy ads ("Bericht: ''") immediately — they're embarrassing the brand and burning budget with zero intent.
• Stop spreading €1-3 across random posts with no conversion objective — consolidate budget behind proven winners.

🇧🇪

Belgium

2 ads · €89 spend · 0 results
✅ What's Working
• Both ads generate absurdly high CTR (122%+ and 110%+), suggesting the creative sparks curiosity and gets clicks — people are interested in workwear.
• Low total spend (€89 combined) means the account hasn't burned serious budget yet — damage is contained.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero results across both ads despite €86+ spend on 120239393986810631 — clicks go nowhere, indicating a broken funnel, dead pixel, or misconfigured conversion event.
• CTRs over 100% are a data red flag — likely duplicate click counting or event misconfiguration, meaning reported engagement may be inflated and unreliable.
• 120239394435940631 got only €3 delivery — Meta's algorithm likely throttled it due to poor predicted conversion rate or audience overlap.
⬆ Double Down On
• Fix tracking and pixel FIRST — no creative strategy matters until conversions actually register. Verify pixel fires, CAPI setup, and conversion event mapping.
• Lean into the click interest: whatever hook is driving those clicks has potential — rebuild the post-click experience (landing page, lead form) to capture that intent.
• Target Belgian B2B decision-makers (facility managers, HR, procurement) with offer-driven creatives — free quote, bulk discount, or sample request.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop spending a single euro until the pixel and conversion tracking are verified end-to-end — you're flying blind.
• Kill the current landing page or funnel — 0 conversions on 100%+ CTR means the post-click experience is fundamentally broken or nonexistent.

Other

8 ads · €7135 spend · 392 results
✅ What's Working
• Calculator lead magnets dominate — "[LEADS] Plat dak | BROAD | Calculator" delivers 120 leads at €12.78 CPR, roughly half the cost of hellend dak equivalents.
• Recruitment ads are absurdly efficient — "Vacature Adviseur Plat Dak" pulls 73 results at €2.91 CPR with 171% outbound CTR, proving strong employer brand.
• Asbestvrij dak angle sustains solid volume (74 leads) at acceptable €27.15 CPR — urgency-driven messaging resonates for hellend dak.
❌ What's Not Working
• "[LEADS] Plat dak | BROAD | Kostprijs 2026" is burning cash — 5 leads at €67.28 CPR is 5x worse than the same audience's Calculator ad. The generic pricing angle fails for plat dak.
• "[LEADS] Plat dak | BROAD | Gratis dakinspectie" has the lowest CTR (47.88%) and only 3 leads — free inspection offer isn't compelling enough to convert cold traffic.
• Hellend dak CPRs across the board (€25-27) are roughly 2x plat dak Calculator — the segment needs stronger creative differentiation.
⬆ Double Down On
• Build more calculator/tool-based lead magnets for every roof type and renovation scenario — the interactive format clearly outperforms static offers.
• Expand the asbestvrij/regulation-urgency angle to plat dak audiences — compliance fear + deadline = high-intent leads.
• Clone the recruitment ad format from "Vacature Adviseur Plat Dak" — test more roles and regions using the same creative structure since it's converting at €2.91.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill "[LEADS] Plat dak | BROAD | Kostprijs 2026" immediately — the Calculator ad serves the same audience at 5x better efficiency.
• Kill "[LEADS] Plat dak | BROAD | Gratis dakinspectie" — worst CTR, worst efficiency, worst volume. Free inspection isn't a compelling enough hook for cold traffic.

Belgium

30 ads · €1855 spend · 15 results
✅ What's Working
• "Static _ Business #1 - Copy" is the clear volume winner: 5 results at €34.83 each — business-benefit static messaging resonates.
• "Static _ Gunther #1" delivers the best CPR among scaled ads (€29.17, 3 results) with a monster 248% CTR — person-led social proof statics crush.
• "Video _ Concierge #3" quietly produced the lowest CPR in the account (€17.63) on minimal spend — a diamond that needs budget.
❌ What's Not Working
• "Video _ Call #2 - Copy" and "Static _ Matthias #1" burned €513 combined for just 2 results at €250+ each — expensive vanity spend.
• Concierge videos #1 and #4 have been tested across multiple ad sets (4 entries total, €173 spent) with zero results — the concept is dead.
• "Static _ Career Advancement #1 - Copy" flopped at €51 with 0 results and the lowest CTR (63%) — wrong angle for this audience.
⬆ Double Down On
• Person-named testimonial statics à la Gunther — this format has the best efficiency and engagement; produce 3-4 more featuring different clients.
• Business-benefit static variants — "Business #1" proves the value-prop framing converts; iterate on copy, layout, and CTA.
• Short-form video in the Concierge #3 style — isolate what made #3 convert while #1 and #4 failed (likely hook/length), and create new cuts.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Concierge #1 and #4 video variants immediately — four instances, zero results, €173 wasted.
• Kill "Static _ Career Advancement #1 - Copy" — wrong message, worst CTR, no traction.
• Stop running "Video _ Call #2 - Copy" and "Static _ Matthias #1" at current CPRs — €250+/result is unsustainable.

🌐

Other

30 ads · €8368 spend · 134 results
✅ What's Working
• Vottem project dominates across all formats — video (€23/result, 30 leads), animatie (€25/result), carousel (€33/result) — proving the project itself has strong demand and creative variety works.
• Native-style ads crush CTA-heavy variants: "Blom_apt_native" (€21.84/result, CTR 298%) vs "Blom_ext_cta" (€58.80/result) — 2.7x more efficient. Same pattern with "Charleroi_native" (€48.63) vs "Charleroi-image-cta - v2" (€92.07).
• "Brugge_penthouse" combines highest CTR in the entire account (382%) with strong volume (21 results at €30.41) — premium product + aspirational creative = winner.
❌ What's Not Working
• Wildebeek is a black hole: €1,293 spent across 3 ads, 1 total result at €498.50. "wildebeek_flexibele units" and its remarketing variant both generated zero results. The messaging and creative are fundamentally broken.
• Awans project is dead on arrival — "Awans_reel" (€219/result, 1 lead) and "ODD Awans 18/8" (€158 spent, 0 results). €377 burned for 1 lead.
• Close-up/detail shots and rental messaging fail hard: "west-closeup" (€176/result) vs "west_ext" (€44/result); "Charleroi_te-huur" (€281/result) vs "Charleroi_native" (€48/result).
⬆ Double Down On
• Video and animation formats for every project — Vottem proves video (30 results) and animation (10 results) outperform static. Roll this format playbook to Brugge, Blom, and West immediately.
• Native-style creatives that blend into feed — the pattern is undeniable across Blom and Charleroi. Kill the CTA-heavy variants and go editorial/organic-looking.
• Penthouse and aspirational lifestyle positioning — Brugge_penthouse's 382% CTR signals massive appetite for premium units. Lead with hero units, not flexible/generic messaging.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• All Wildebeek ads immediately — €1,293 wasted. The "flexibele units" angle clearly doesn't resonate. Full creative and messaging overhaul needed before any re-launch.
• Both Awans ads — €377 for 1 result. The reel format and ODD event concept both failed. Stop the bleeding.
• "Charleroi_te-huur" — rental positioning at €281/result vs €49 for the same project's native ad. The audience doesn't convert on rental CTAs at this cost.

✅ What's Working
• "Static _ Doorstromer #1 - Copy" is the runaway winner: 122 results at €5.47 each — dwarfs every other ad in volume and efficiency.
• Alleenstaand segment converts well when the right creative hits: "Static _ Alleenstaand #1" (€210 variant, 20 results at €10.52) and "Static _ Alleenstaand #2" (€480 variant, 31 results at €15.49) both deliver.
• The "- Copy" variants consistently crush their originals (Doorstromer #1 Copy at €5.47 vs original at €160.03; Doorstromer #2 Copy at €13.12 vs original at €42.69), suggesting the copy/audience tweaks in those variants are the real drivers.
❌ What's Not Working
• Algemeen (general) targeting is a budget sinkhole: across 7 Algemeen ad entries totalling ~€633, only 8 results were generated — multiple variants delivered zero results at meaningful spend.
• Original creatives without the "Copy" suffix underperform catastrophically: "Static _ Doorstromer #1" burned €640 for only 4 results (€160 each), and "Static _ Alleenstaand #2" (€196 variant) spent nearly €200 for 1 result.
• Jong Koppel ads are starved and stalling: 5 entries, mostly zero results, with only the low-spend "Jong Koppel #1 - Copy" (€14, 1 result) showing any sign of life.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more Doorstromer creative variants — this audience converts cheapest and at highest volume. Test new angles, formats, and hooks specifically for this segment.
• Replicate the "Copy" variant approach across all segments: whatever targeting or copy adjustment those variants carry is the difference between €5 and €160 per result.
• Invest more in the Alleenstaand segment with fresh creatives — it's the clear #2 segment and still has room to scale at sub-€16 cost/result.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Algemeen ads immediately. General targeting is burning budget with almost no conversions.
• Pause every original (non-Copy) variant that has a Copy counterpart outperforming it — they're cannibalizing budget from proven winners.
• Stop running Jong Koppel ads at current creative quality — 0-result entries across multiple instances prove the creative doesn't resonate with this audience.

3 ads · €299 spend · 5 results
✅ What's Working
• "PVC. VER.- PUB CONVERTION - 2026" shows a €5.5 cost/result — 13x cheaper than the pergola ad on tiny spend, signaling PVC-specific messaging resonates.
• The 2026 forward-planning angle appears in both result-generating ads, suggesting seasonal pre-booking hooks engage this audience.
• All three ads show abnormally high CTRs (142-168%), indicating the creative formats are stopping thumbs — engagement is not the problem.
❌ What's Not Working
• "VERANDAS - PUB CONVERTIONS" burned €8 with zero results and the vaguest product framing — generic category names don't convert.
• "PERGOLAS - PUB CONVERTIONS - 2026" ate 95% of budget (€286) but delivered only 4 results at €71.46 each — massive click-to-conversion drop means the post-click experience or offer is broken.
• Zero ROAS tracking across all ads — you're spending blind on high-ticket products with no revenue attribution whatsoever.
⬆ Double Down On
• Product-specific creatives with tight naming (PVC verandas, bioclimatic pergolas, aluminum extensions) — the PVC ad's €5.5 CPR proves specificity wins over generic.
• 2026 pre-booking / early-bird angle — both converting ads use it; lean into scarcity and planning timelines for big-ticket home improvements.
• Low-spend rapid testing — the PVC ad proved a signal on just €6; run more €20-€50 micro-tests on new product angles before committing budget.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running any ad without proper conversion tracking and ROAS attribution — you're selling €10K+ products with zero revenue visibility.
• Kill the generic "VERANDAS" positioning entirely — it says nothing specific, differentiates nothing, converts nobody.
• Stop pouring budget into "PERGOLAS" at €71.46/result until post-click funnel (landing page, form, CTA) is diagnosed and fixed.

✅ What's Working
• CARPORTS is the clear winner — 6 results at €9.26/result, best efficiency across the account by a wide margin.
• PERGOLAS - PUB CONVERTIONS is generating leads at €20.55 but proving the pergola category converts on Meta.
• High CTRs across all ads (195-266%) suggest strong creative engagement — the visuals/hooks are grabbing attention.
❌ What's Not Working
• VERANDAS PUB CONVERTION - Copie has the highest CTR (266%) but zero conversions — classic disconnect between click bait and conversion intent. Landing page or offer is likely broken.
• Overall budget allocation is backwards: the best performer (CARPORTS) gets less spend than the weaker one (PERGOLAS). No scaling logic in place.
• Zero ROAS tracking across all campaigns — flying completely blind on revenue attribution.
⬆ Double Down On
• Carport-focused creatives — the category converts at half the cost of pergolas, exploit this demand signal with more creative variations.
• Product-specific conversion campaigns — each product line (carport, pergola, veranda) needs its own tailored funnel, not generic copy-paste ads.
• Before/after transformation content — outdoor living projects are inherently visual; leverage completed project photography to drive qualified leads.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running the VERANDAS Copie ad without fixing the post-click experience — 266% CTR with zero results means you're paying for curiosity clicks that go nowhere.
• Stop spreading €3-€10 across campaigns — either fund them properly (€20+/day minimum) or don't run them at all. Micro-budgets starve the algorithm.
• Stop ignoring ROAS tracking — without value-based signals, Meta cannot optimize for actual revenue.

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no results

🌐

Other

30 ads · €7753 spend · 283 results
✅ What's Working
• Carousel pergola format is the workhorse — PERGOLA_CARROUSEL_MUTLI4 variants drive 108 results across instances, best at €16.51 CPR. Proven scalable.
• Simple conversion-focused creatives win — VERANDAS - PUB CONVERTIONS - Copie (€20.12 CPR), PUB PERGOLAS 2 (€20.18), PUB CARPORT 1 (€20.78) all cluster under €21. No gimmicks, just direct response.
• Video format shows promise on niche products — PVCS_VIDEO_MUTLI3 delivers €18.25 CPR with the highest engagement (293% CTR metric), proving video can unlock underperforming categories like PVC.
❌ What's Not Working
• Verancobel-branded standalone ads are a money pit — PVC VERANCOBEL (€61.73 CPR), VERANDA VERANCOBEL (€49.98), PERGOLA VERANCOBEL (€32.95). Brand-first creative kills conversion efficiency across every product line.
• PERGOLA_CARROUSEL_RJF7 burned €676 for only 10 results at €67.65 CPR — worst efficiency in the account, likely a bad creative variant cannibalizing the working carousel.
• PVC as a category is bleeding except when in video — PUB PVC 3 at €53.29 CPR with only 4 results on €213 spend. Static PVC creative does not convert.
⬆ Double Down On
• Carousel format across ALL product lines — it works for pergolas, now replicate the structure for carports, verandas, and PVC. Multi-image showing product range is your best format.
• Direct-response 'PUB' style creatives — the simple, conversion-optimized naming pattern correlates with sub-€21 CPRs. Produce more variants in this no-frills, benefit-led style.
• Video for underperforming categories — PVCS_VIDEO_MUTLI3 proves video rescues weak categories. Apply this to carports and verandas where static is plateauing.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Verancobel-branded standalone ads immediately — VERANDA VERANCOBEL, PVC VERANCOBEL, PERGOLA VERANCOBEL. Brand awareness is not converting and there is no ROAS data to justify it.
• Kill PERGOLA_CARROUSEL_RJF7 — it is a broken variant eating budget the working MUTLI4 carousel should absorb.
• Kill PUB PVC 3 — static PVC does not work; video does. Stop throwing money at a dead format for this product.

Other

7 ads · €1294 spend · 35 results
✅ What's Working
• "IZWVL - Algemeen - Visual" is the sole result-generator (35 results at €13.27) — broad, non-location-specific creative converts where influencer-x-location ads do not.
• High engagement rates across the board (30-290% CTR) indicate the IZWVL brand concept and provincial domains genuinely interest the audience — awareness is not the problem.
• The general/umbrella creative approach outperforms hyper-specific influencer-location pairings, suggesting users want a menu of options, not a single destination pitch.
❌ What's Not Working
• Every influencer-x-location ad (Chloe-Bulskampveld, Magnolia-Phof, TheLifePlanFamily-Palingbeek, Magnolia-Raversyde, Hannes-Duinpanne) produced exactly ZERO results on a combined €828 spend — the funnel from engagement to action is completely broken.
• The conversion mechanism on location-specific ads is failing: high CTR but 0 results points to either a misaligned campaign objective, a broken landing page/CTA, or audiences engaging with content but seeing no reason to take the next step.
• "IZWVL - Algemeen - GIF" received only €1 — it was essentially never tested, making it dead weight in the account.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more general/umbrella creatives that showcase multiple provincial domains in one ad, mirroring the winning "Algemeen - Visual" format — give users choice, not a single destination.
• Shift influencer content from standalone location ads to supporting roles inside broader creatives (e.g., influencer highlights stitched into a carousel of 3-4 domains).
• Invest in fixing the conversion path: audit landing pages for each domain, ensure CTAs are clear (book a visit, plan your route, download the app) and the pixel/event tracking is correctly firing on location-specific pages.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running influencer-x-single-location ads in their current form — €828 spent with zero results is a clear signal the format does not convert.
• Kill the orphaned "IZWVL - Algemeen - GIF" ad — at €1 spend it was never properly launched and is cluttering the account.

🇧🇪

Belgium

12 ads · €76 spend · 17 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Static formats crush it: "Static _ Cover #1" (75.83x ROAS, €0.70 CPP) and "Static _ Key Visual #1" (13.36x ROAS, 7 purchases) are the workhorses — simple, clear, high-converting.
• Urgency/scarcity messaging converts: "Video _ Ticket Update #1" drove 5 purchases at 11.39x ROAS — countdown-style ticket pressure clearly resonates for event sales.
• Story-format videos show outsized efficiency: both "Video _ Story #1" variants delivered 26-34x ROAS at sub-€5 CPP despite minimal spend.
❌ What's Not Working
• "Video _ Key Visual #1" is the video version of your best static — €2 in, zero purchases. Static outperforms the animated treatment of the same concept.
• Massive under-spending across the board: 8 of 12 ads got ≤€1. You cannot learn anything from €1 of spend. This isn't an ad problem, it's a budget allocation problem.
• No ad has enough spend to build real statistical confidence — even the top spender ("Static _ Key Visual #1") only spent €38.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more static key visuals and covers — they convert at the lowest CPP and highest ROAS. Make 3-4 new variants immediately.
• Lean hard into urgency/scarcity hooks: "Ticket Update" and "Last 250" framing directly addresses FOMO — create more countdown and limited-availability creatives.
• Scale Story-format vertical videos — both "Video _ Story #1" entries show exceptional ROAS efficiency; feed this format more budget and more variants.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop spreading €1 across 6+ ads. Consolidate budget behind proven winners or you'll learn nothing and sell nothing.
• Kill the video version of key visuals — "Video _ Key Visual #1" adds production cost for worse results than its static twin.
